name: Orvex Tactical MA-2 Bomber
description:
A militarized update of the classic MA-1 bomber silhouette, manufactured by Orvex for the private security and civilian tactical markets. The shell is a tight-weave ballistic nylon in matte olive or slate grey, and the interior is lined with a bright safety-orange synth-satin — the traditional reversal lining, kept for historical continuity. Ribbed knit collar, cuffs, and waistband. Multiple zip pockets including a secure document sleeve sewn into the left chest panel. The cut is boxy but not oversized — room to layer, room to move.

Orvex doesn't advertise to civilians, but the MA-2 has become a staple of Tier 2 security work and Tier 3 urban-casual wear simultaneously. Private site guards buy it for function; younger residents buy it for the silhouette and the association. The jacket carries no overt branding — just a small woven label inside the collar. On the Shelf, a secondhand MA-2 is considered a score.
what_it_says: You're either in security, adjacent to security, or you want people to wonder. The lack of branding does most of the work.
story_hooks: Orvex has a standing contract with three corponations for uniformed security jackets — but those contracts require a specific internal RFID tag that can be used to track wearer location. Civilian versions don't have it. Or so the packaging claims.

A counterfeit MA-2 market has emerged on the Shelf — the fakes are actually decent quality, made in unlicensed shops, and missing the document sleeve. How you tell them apart matters if you're buying for real security work.
A former Orvex quality inspector was fired after flagging a materials substitution in a corporate order. She kept a sample of the substandard lining. She wants someone to care about it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A structured, utilitarian silhouette with military heritage. Boxy through the torso with tapered sleeves, sitting between vintage and contemporary tactical wear. The matte finish reads as no-nonsense professional, while the bright orange lining visible at the collar and cuffs hints at functional excess. Projects competence and restraint.
physical_description.fit: Boxy and deliberately roomy through the chest and shoulders, allowing for layered augmentation ports or armor inserts. Tapered at the wrists with ribbed cuffs that seal snugly. Sits at hip length. Cut to accommodate movement and additional gear without bagginess.
physical_description.primary_material: Tight-weave ballistic nylon shell — matte finish, durable synthetic rated for impact and abrasion resistance. Synth-satin safety-orange lining for visibility and historical aesthetic continuity.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly stiff ballistic nylon with subtle grid weave visible under close inspection. Ribbed knit collar, cuffs, and waistband offer tactile warmth and secure fit. Lining is slick, allowing easy layering.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte olive or slate grey exterior. Bright safety-orange interior lining creates striking contrast when jacket is worn open or when sleeves are rolled. No pattern; solid, functional colorway.
physical_description.closures: Central front full-length zipper with metal slider. Multiple zip pockets: two hand-entry side pockets, secure document sleeve on left chest with reinforced stitching and concealed zip.
distinctive_features: Bright safety-orange synth-satin reversal lining — a nod to vintage MA-1 bombers, maintained for brand continuity
Reinforced chest document sleeve with internal organization
Minimal branding — only small woven label inside collar, no logos or visible Φ pricing
Ribbed knit in contrasting texture at collar, cuffs, waistband
Ballistic nylon shell designed for durability and minimal maintenance
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 crossover. Expensive enough for dedicated security professionals (Tier 2 corpo contractors), but accessible enough and aesthetically valued by working-class Tier 3 residents as aspirational tactical wear.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals pragmatism, security work, or deliberate style-referencing. Worn by private site guards, corporate security detail, and younger residents who value the silhouette's historical weight and functional aesthetic. Carries subtle status — not flashy, but recognized. On the Shelf (secondhand market), it's a valued find indicating taste and access.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually purchased pristine and broken in over months. Well-maintained examples show minimal wear; heavily used examples develop creasing at elbows and collar, slight fading on high-friction areas. Patched versions are not uncommon in Tier 3 wear.
